articles.title: A Small English Town Could Decide the Next Prime Minister—Here's How
articles.summary: Makerfield, a constituency of 76,000 voters near Wigan, is suddenly the stage for a high-stakes by-election. Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham is running for Parliament, hoping to challenge PM Keir Starmer. But Reform UK, led by Nigel Farage, is mounting an aggressive campaign.

articles.title: 250,000 Daily Riders Face Chaos as LIRR Strike Deadline Looms
articles.summary: North America's busiest commuter railroad, the Long Island Rail Road, could shut down at 12:01 a.m. Saturday if unions and the MTA fail to agree on a new contract. Five unions representing 3,500 workers are seeking higher raises. The MTA has offered a 9.5% increase over three years plus a potential fourth-year lump sum.

articles.title: Gen Z Defies the Odds: How Some 20-Somethings Are Buying Homes in an Unaffordable Market
articles.summary: At 27, Francisco Vazquez bought a $220,000 home in Milwaukee after saving $72,000 in two years. He's part of a growing Gen Z homeownership trend, with 4% of buyers now from that generation. They're more likely to be single, female, and financially independent than millennials were.
